summary:
AFTER EARTH is an interactive 3D experience which brings the stories of the forgotten equipment of space exploration to life. It's aimed at students and space fans and allows you to walk around the Moon and Mars, go to the actual locations of the missions and find the machines that we left there.
Via immersive environments, interactive maps and animations showing how the equipment got there and how it operated, users can get a real sense of not just what the machines were, but what missions they were on and what discoveries they enabled.
Our project is about making the history of space missions more interesting and accessible to younger people. Instead of just presenting the facts in a text book style we're going to turn the history of space into an experience that sparks interest and encourages people to explore. The aim is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers and space explorers to ask the questions that lead to all the great discoveries.
details:
What it does. AFTER EARTH is a first-person 3D journey to eight real landing sites. Visitors choose the Moon or Mars, land at true coordinates, and explore on foot. Glowing beacons lead to ten artifacts: Apollo 11's Eagle descent stage and laser retroreflector, Surveyor 3, the Apollo 15 rover, Apollo 17's Challenger, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder, Sojourner, Opportunity and InSight. Each has a dossier what it is, purpose, mission, how it worked, discoveries, current status and facts plus numbered parts to inspect,and an ending screen sums up the journey.

How it works. It is a website written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript using three.js for 3D graphics. Official NASA 3D models are used for the Lunar Module, Viking 1, Opportunity and InSight. Equipment is placed at documented distances, such as Apollo 12 landing about 160 m from Surveyor 3. Sound is generated live with the Web Audio API, and phones get touch controls, a joystick and tilt-to-look.

Benefits and goals. It is free, needs no install or login, and works on the phones students carry. It connects engineering to discovery and helps young people see these machines as explorers with stories , inspiring the generation that will return to the Moon with Artemis.

Tools. HTML, CSS, JavaScript, three.js, Web Audio API, Device Orientation API, NASA 3D Resources, GitHub Pages, and Claude as an AI assistant.

My role. I came up with the concept and wrote the full design plan — the 3D home screen, Moon/Mars choice, first-person exploration, map, information panel, "The Past" animations and ending. I chose the sites, machines and stories, decided to use official NASA models and real distances, tested it on phone and computer, directed every improvement, and published it on GitHub Pages.
